findings: An infiltrative pancreatic cancer measuring 58 mm is observed in the body of the pancreas. Serosal invasion and retropancreatic tissue invasion are noted. There is contact of more than 180° with both the superior mesenteric vein and the splenic vein, suggesting invasion. Superior mesenteric vein invasion extends beyond the inferior border of the duodenum. Stenosis of the splenic artery is observed, raising suspicion of invasion. No other local invasion factors are identified. No lymph node metastases are present. Multiple nodular shadows are observed in both lungs, raising suspicion of multiple lung metastases.

responses.content:
Task 1: Diagnose the local invasion factors of pancreatic cancer.

CH0 (no invasion of the common hepatic artery)
DU1 (invasion of the duodenum)
S1 (serosal invasion)
RP1 (retropancreatic tissue invasion)
PV1 (invasion of the portal vein)
A1 (invasion of the splenic artery)
PL0 (no invasion of the pancreatic lymphatic vessels)
OO1 (invasion of the omentum)

Task 2: Determine the classification for local invasion (T classification) of pancreatic cancer.

Based on the size of the tumor (58 mm) and the presence of serosal invasion, retropancreatic tissue invasion, and invasion of the portal vein and splenic artery, the T classification is T3.

Task 3: Determine the N classification of pancreatic cancer.

Regional lymph nodes for pancreatic cancer in the body of the pancreas are:
- Station 12 (left gastric artery)
- Station 13 (common hepatic artery)
- Station 14 (proper hepatic artery)
- Station 17 (splenic artery)
- Station 18 (splenic artery)
- Station 19 (hilar lymph nodes)
- Station 14a (gastroduodenal artery)
- Station 14b (right gastric artery)
- Station 14c (common bile duct)

No metastatic lymph nodes are present in these regional stations. Therefore, the N classification is N0.

Task 4: Determine the M classification of pancreatic cancer.

Multiple nodular shadows are observed in both lungs, raising suspicion of multiple lung metastases. Therefore, the M classification is M1.

Task 5: Determine the resectability classification of pancreatic cancer.

Based on the presence of distant metastases (M1), the resectability classification is Unresectable (UR).

Task 6: Determine the overall stage according to the JPS staging system.

Based on the T classification (T3), N classification (N0), and M classification (M1), the overall stage is Stage IV.
